title: Publication Architecture, Facing Pages, Slug & Bleed Standards
subtitle: Commercial Print Geometry, Binding Gutters & Press-Ready Margins

learningObjectives: Understand the mechanics of commercial editorial printing: signatures, facing page spreads, and spine creep.
Configure facing pages, starting page sides (Right vs Left), and page counts matching commercial binding multiples (4s/8s/16s).
Calculate and configure 3mm ISO standard bleed zones and explain why bleed is non-negotiable for edge-to-edge color.
Establish asymmetrical margins with binding gutter allowances for perfect bound vs saddle-stitched publications.
standardSections.foundationalKnowledge: In digital document production, a single screen page is self-contained. In commercial print production, documents are printed on giant parent sheets (press sheets), folded into multi-page bundles called 'signatures' (typically 8, 16, or 32 pages), bound together, and mechanically trimmed with high-speed guillotines. Because paper shifts slightly during mechanical folding and trimming (tolerance of +/- 1.0mm), any artwork intended to touch the paper's edge must extend beyond the trim line into a designated 3.0mm 'Bleed' zone. Failure to include bleed results in unsightly slivers of unprinted white paper along trimmed edges.

technicalEvidence.source: Affinity Publisher Document Architecture, ISO 12647 Bleed & Trim Specifications

toolAndFeatureExplanation.description: Accessed via File > Document Setup (Ctrl+Shift+P / Cmd+Shift+P) or during initial document creation. Controls page dimensions, facing page flow, margins, bleed zones, and color management.
contextBarOptions: Facing Pages Checkbox: Creates side-by-side spreads (Left/Right) sharing a central spine
Arrange Dropdown: Horizontal (Standard book spreads) or Vertical
Start On: Right (Standard editorial start—Page 1 is front right cover)
Bleed Inputs: Top, Bottom, Inner, Outer (Standard 3.0 mm on all exterior edges)

stepByStepInstructions.title: Launch New Publication Dialog
stepByStepInstructions.instruction: Open Affinity Publisher and press Ctrl+N (Windows) / Cmd+N (macOS). Under the 'Print' or 'Press Ready' category, select preset 'A4' (210 x 297 mm).

stepByStepInstructions.title: Configure Facing Page Architecture
stepByStepInstructions.instruction: Under the 'Layout' tab on the right, check the box labeled 'Facing pages'. Set 'Arrange' to Horizontal, and 'Start on' to 'Right'. Set initial Pages to 8 (a standard 8-page introductory signature).

stepByStepInstructions.title: Set Asymmetrical Binding Margins
stepByStepInstructions.instruction: Click the 'Margins' tab. Uncheck the chain-link icon to allow independent margin values. Set Top: 20mm, Bottom: 22mm, Outer: 18mm, and Inner (Gutter): 25mm. Notice how the inner gutter provides essential clearance so text doesn't disappear into the folded spine.

stepByStepInstructions.title: Configure 3mm Commercial Bleed
stepByStepInstructions.instruction: Click the 'Bleed' tab. Ensure the chain-link icon is checked and enter '3.0 mm'. All four fields (Top, Bottom, Inner, Outer) will populate with 3mm. Click 'Create'.

stepByStepInstructions.title: Verify Bleed Guides on Canvas
stepByStepInstructions.instruction: Look at your newly created spread. The solid border is the page Trim line. The outer cyan/gray guideline extending 3mm beyond the edge is the Bleed line. Ensure background artwork extends all the way to this outer bleed line.

visualExamples.title: Binding Methods vs Gutter Requirements
visualExamples.description: Recommended gutter allowances by binding type.
visualExamples.visualContent:
| Binding Style | Page Range | Gutter Recommendation | Production Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| Saddle-Stitched | 8 - 64 pages | 15 mm - 18 mm | Wire staples through spine; lays relatively flat |
| Perfect Bound | 48 - 400+ pages | 22 mm - 28 mm | Glued square spine; requires deep gutter for reading |
| Case Bound (Hardcover) | 80+ pages | 25 mm - 32 mm | Stitched signatures encased in board; large hinge allowance |
| Wire-O / Spiral | Any | 20 mm - 24 mm | Punched holes through inner margin; keep text clear |

commonPitfalls.pitfall: Snapping artwork to the page edge instead of the bleed line
commonPitfalls.cause: Assuming the visible canvas edge is where color should stop.
commonPitfalls.solution: Always pull background fills and images past the black page border out to the red/cyan bleed line. When the print house cuts the paper, any slight blade deviation will cut colored ink, not white paper.

commonPitfalls.pitfall: Symmetrical margins causing text to be swallowed by the spine
commonPitfalls.cause: Setting all margins to a uniform 15mm in a thick book.
commonPitfalls.solution: Always use asymmetrical margins: make the Inner (Gutter) margin substantially wider (22-28mm) than the Outer margin (15-18mm) for perfect bound books.

commonPitfalls.pitfall: Page counts that cannot be bound
commonPitfalls.cause: Submitting a 19-page document for saddle-stitched print.
commonPitfalls.solution: Commercial sheet-fed printing folds 1 sheet of paper into 4 pages. Print page counts MUST be multiples of 4 (e.g. 8, 12, 16, 20, 24, 28, 32).

knowledgeCheck.question: Why must print artwork that touches the edge of a page extend into the 3mm Bleed zone?
options: To increase the overall resolution of the PDF.

Because mechanical guillotine blades have physical cutting tolerances (+/- 1mm); extending color into the bleed zone ensures that slight trimming shifts never leave an unprinted white sliver along the edge.
Because ink cannot stick to the exact edge of paper.
knowledgeCheck.explanation: Bleed provides an intentional margin of error for industrial print finishing, ensuring clean, borderless color even if paper slips slightly under the blade.

knowledgeCheck.question: Why should the Inner (Gutter) margin of a perfect-bound book be wider than the Outer margin?
options: It makes the book lighter to hold.
Because the inner spine of a perfect bound book is glued together and bends into the binding valley; extra gutter margin ensures readable text is not obscured by the page curvature.
Because left pages have less text than right pages.
It is an arbitrary tradition with no practical purpose.
knowledgeCheck.explanation: In glued perfect-bound books, pages do not lay completely flat. Text placed too close to the spine curves into the gutter and becomes illegible.

knowledgeCheck.question: Why must the page count of a standard saddle-stitched commercial publication be a multiple of 4?
options: Because Affinity Publisher only counts in 4s.
Because each physical sheet of paper folded in half creates exactly 4 individual pages (front-left, front-right, back-left, back-right).
Because printers charge by sets of four.
knowledgeCheck.explanation: Folding any single sheet of physical paper in half creates 2 leaves, which equals exactly 4 numbered pages. Therefore, signature binding requires multiples of 4.

summaryPoints: Publication architecture requires understanding commercial press mechanics (signatures and folding).
Facing pages allow editorial designers to balance typography and visual weight across full spreads.
Commercial 3mm bleed prevents white paper slivers caused by guillotine trimming shifts.
Asymmetrical gutter margins safeguard legibility against spine curvature in glued books.

slides.title: Publication Architecture & Bleed Standards
slides.subtitle: The Engineering Behind Commercial Print Layout
slides.contentMarkdown:
Welcome to **Affinity Publisher 3.0**.

Designing for print is an engineering discipline: you are not creating a static digital screen—you are creating a physical three-dimensional object made of folded, glued, and trimmed paper.

In this lesson, you will master **facing page spreads, spine gutter physics, and the non-negotiable rules of 3mm commercial bleed**.

actionBox.label: Print Truth
actionBox.text: Every printed book is made of folded sheets. Page counts must always be multiples of 4.

slides.title: Facing Pages & The Anatomy of a Spread
slides.subtitle: Viewing the Reader's Eye Flow
slides.contentMarkdown:
When you open a book or magazine, you never read a single page in isolation:

- You view **two facing pages simultaneously (a Spread)**.
- **Page 1 (Front Cover):** Sits alone on the **Right**.
- **Pages 2 & 3:** First interior spread (Page 2 Left, Page 3 Right), meeting at the center **Spine**.
- **Final Page (Back Cover):** Sits alone on the **Left**.

slides.title: Document Setup: Margins & Bleed Engine
slides.subtitle: Configuring Precision Geometry
slides.contentMarkdown:
In `File > Document Setup` (Ctrl+Shift+P / Cmd+Shift+P):

- **Facing Pages:** Check `[x] Facing pages`.
- **Start on:** Set to `Right`.
- **Margins:** Uncheck uniform linking. Set Inner (Gutter) to `25mm` to clear the binding curve. Set Outer to `18mm`.
- **Bleed:** Set to `3.0 mm` on all sides.
- **Color Profile:** Ensure commercial CMYK (e.g. `Coated FOGRA39`).

actionBox.label: Commercial Rule
actionBox.text: Standard European and Asian commercial offset printers require 3.0mm bleed. US printers typically require 0.125 inches (3.175mm).

slides.title: Step-by-Step: Setting Up an 8-Page Magazine Spread
slides.subtitle: From Blank Canvas to Press-Ready Signature
slides.contentMarkdown:
1. **Initialize:** Press `Ctrl+N` (Win) / `Cmd+N` (Mac). Choose `Print > A4`.
2. **Enable Spreads:** Check `Facing pages`, set `Start on: Right`, and set `Number of pages: 8`.
3. **Set Margins:** Unlink margins. Top: `20mm`, Bottom: `22mm`, Inner: `25mm`, Outer: `18mm`.
4. **Set Bleed:** In the Bleed tab, enter `3.0 mm` across all edges.
5. **Create & Inspect:** Click Create. Open the Pages studio on the left. Notice your cover page on the right, followed by 3 two-page interior spreads!
6. **Extend Color to Bleed:** Place a color block and drag it past the black edge until it snaps to the outer red bleed line.

visual.content: View > View Mode > Clip to Canvas (Ctrl+W / Cmd+W) toggles between showing bleed and previewing final trimmed paper.

slides.title: Print Production Pitfalls & Traps
slides.subtitle: Avoid Costly Reprints
slides.contentMarkdown:
### 1. The White Sliver of Shame
- **Cause:** Snapping a photo to the black page edge instead of the red 3mm bleed guide.
- **Result:** Trimming blades shift 0.5mm, leaving an ugly white paper hairline on the final print.
- **Fix:** Always pull bleeds to the outer guide line.

### 2. Swallowed Spine Text
- **Cause:** Using equal 12mm margins everywhere. In a 200-page book, text curves into the spine and becomes unreadable.
- **Fix:** Give the Inner margin at least 25mm to 28mm for perfect binding.

### 3. Odd Page Counts
- **Rule:** A booklet cannot have 15 or 17 pages. Always ensure your page count divides evenly by 4.

actionBox.label: Golden Rule
actionBox.text: If it bleeds, it must extend 3mm past the trim.

slides.title: Independent Challenge: Luxury Editorial Spread
slides.subtitle: Building a Real Magazine Base
slides.contentMarkdown:
### Your Mission:
Construct an 8-page editorial publication architecture in Affinity Publisher:

1. Set up an **A4 portrait document** with Facing Pages, starting on Right.
2. Configure Margins: Top `20mm`, Bottom `24mm`, Outer `18mm`, Inner `26mm`.
3. Configure standard `3.0 mm` bleed.
4. On Spread 2-3 (Pages 2 & 3), place a dark charcoal background rectangle `#111115` spanning the full width of both pages, extending completely to the outer bleed line on all exterior sides.

### Acceptance Criteria:
- 8 total pages organized into 1 cover, 3 spreads, and 1 back cover.
- Spanning rectangle extends exactly to the 3mm bleed line.
- Inner gutter provides 26mm safe margin.
